name: Bucharest: Dracula's Castle, Peleș Castle & Brașov Tour
tagline: Dracula's castle, Romania's grandest palace, and a medieval Saxon city — three of Transylvania's greatest sites in one day from Bucharest
overview: Romania's most iconic day trip from Bucharest covers three world-class destinations in a single extraordinary day: Bran Castle — the Gothic fortress perched on a rock in Transylvania, linked to the Dracula legend — the neo-Renaissance masterpiece of Peleș Castle in Sinaia, and the cobblestone streets of medieval Brașov. All three sites are included in the route; entrance tickets to Bran Castle and Peleș Castle are available as an add-on at booking and are strongly recommended — GYG notes that on-site ticket availability cannot be guaranteed and they advise booking with tickets included. Note that Peleș Castle is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays; on those days it may be viewable from the exterior only.
highlights: Bran Castle — Transylvania's most dramatic Gothic fortress on a 60-metre rock above the mountain pass, linked to Bram Stoker's Dracula legend
Peleș Castle — Romania's most opulent royal palace, built for King Carol I, with 160 gilded rooms and a famous armoury (closed Mon/Tue)
Brașov Old Town — one of the finest medieval Saxon cities in Eastern Europe, with the Black Church and Strada Republicii
Round-trip transport from Bucharest with a licensed local guide
Entrance ticket add-on available at booking — strongly recommended as on-site availability is not guaranteed

itinerary.description: Early morning departure from Bucharest heading northwest through the foothills of the Carpathians toward Transylvania. Your guide introduces the history of Transylvania — the former Principality that sat between the Ottoman and Habsburg empires for three centuries — and the Dracula connection: Bram Stoker's 1897 novel was researched from library books in London and Whitby, never from a visit to Romania, yet his description of the fictional count's castle closely matched Bran's profile.

Bran Castle rises on a 60-metre limestone rock at the Bran Pass between Transylvania and Wallachia — a series of levels connected by narrow staircases, wooden galleries, hidden passages and a shaft through the rock to an underground well. The rooms are furnished with Central European antiques from the 14th to 19th centuries. The castle's most poignant resident was Queen Marie of Romania, granddaughter of Queen Victoria, who fell in love with Bran in 1920 and restored it as her summer residence. Her golden heart casket is displayed in the castle chapel. Entrance ticket: included as add-on at booking, or payable on site (subject to availability).

Peleș Castle in Sinaia is Romania's most extraordinary palace — a neo-Renaissance mountain residence built for King Carol I between 1873 and 1914, with 160 rooms decorated in a fusion of European styles: Flemish tapestries, gilded ceilings, Moorish halls, and an armoury housing the royal weapon collection. The grounds alone are magnificent. Note: Peleș is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays; on those days visits are limited to the exterior and grounds. Entrance ticket: included as add-on at booking, or payable on site (subject to availability).
itinerary.extra_fee: Entrance tickets NOT included by default — add at booking. GYG strongly advises booking with tickets: on-site ticket availability for Bran Castle and Peleș Castle is limited and cannot be guaranteed.

itinerary.description: Free exploration of Brașov, one of the best-preserved medieval Saxon cities in Eastern Europe. Walk the cobbled Strada Republicii to Council Square (Piața Sfatului), visit the Black Church — the largest Gothic church in Eastern Europe — and take in views over the red-roofed old town from the city walls. The city was founded by Teutonic Knights in the 13th century and retains its medieval street plan largely intact.

faqs.question: Are castle entrance tickets included in the price?
faqs.answer: Not by default. Entrance tickets to Bran Castle and Peleș Castle are available as an add-on when booking through GYG. The operator strongly recommends adding them at booking — they note that on-site ticket availability is limited and cannot be guaranteed, particularly in peak season. Book with tickets included to avoid disappointment.

faqs.question: Is Bran Castle really Dracula's castle?
faqs.answer: The connection is based on resemblance, not fact. Bram Stoker researched his 1897 novel from library books in London and Whitby and never visited Romania. His description of the fictional count's castle matches Bran's profile closely enough — a castle on a rocky crag at a mountain pass in Transylvania — that the association was adopted by Romanian tourism. The real Vlad the Impaler may have passed through or been briefly imprisoned at Bran in 1462, but never lived there. The castle's real human story — centred on Queen Marie of Romania — is arguably more interesting.

faqs.question: Why is Peleș Castle closed on certain days?
faqs.answer: Peleș Castle is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays year-round for maintenance and administrative purposes. On closed days, visitors can walk the grounds and view the exterior. If interior access to Peleș is your priority, check the day of the week before booking — midweek and weekend tours (Wednesday through Sunday) are guaranteed to include the interior visit.
